rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla rebukes and repudiates the unbelievers' conduct.
rows.anchor: ردع لهم عن ذلك وإنكار لفعلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dakkan dakka means repeated blows until the earth becomes scattered dust.
rows.anchor: كرر عليها الدك حتى عادت هباء منبثا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat recalls people's regret for what they neglected when regret can no longer help.
rows.anchor: ثم أتي بالوعيد وذكر تحسرهم على ما فرطوا فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawma'idhin is appositional to idha dukkat, and both are governed by yatadhakkaru.
rows.anchor: ويومئذ بدل من { إذا دكت الارض } وعامل النصب فيهما { يتذكر }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's coming depicts the display of His power and sovereignty, like a king's arrival displaying awe beyond that of all his forces.
rows.anchor: هو تمثيل لظهور آيات اقتداره وتبين آثار قهره وسلطانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels from each heaven descend rank after rank, surrounding jinn and humans.
rows.anchor: ينزل ملائكة كل سماء فيصطفون صفا بعد صف محدقين بالجن والإنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bringing of Hell is compared with its exposure in 79:36.
rows.anchor: كقوله : { وبرزت الجحيم } ( النازعات : 36 )

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: After revelation the Prophet's face changed; he said Hell would be led by seventy thousand angels with seventy thousand reins and would bolt if released.
rows.anchor: قال : يجيء بها سبعون ألف ملك يقودونها بسبعين ألف زمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person may recall past failures or take admonition; asking how remembrance can help requires supplying an omitted word.
rows.anchor: أي : يتذكر ما فرط فيه ، أو يتعظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “I sent ahead for my life” can mean the afterlife or one's time alive in this world; the former is clearer and implies human choice, not compulsion.
rows.anchor: هذه ، وهي حياة الآخرة ، أو وقت حياتي في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the active reading, the pronoun may refer to the person or Ubayy ibn Khalaf: none suffers or bears punishment like him, as in 17:15.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو أبي بن خلف أي : لا يعذب أحد مثل عذابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the passive reading, the pronoun can refer to God, whose punishment none administers, or to the human, whose tormentors punish no one as severely.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بالكسر ، والضمير لله تعالى ، أي : لا يتولى عذاب الله أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is an implied divine saying to the believer, spoken directly in honor as with Moses or through an angel.
rows.anchor: على إرادة القول ، أي : يقول الله للمؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tranquil soul is secure from fear and grief, or a believing soul settled in truth by certainty; Ubayy's reading supports the first sense.
rows.anchor: المطمئنة } الآمنة التي لا يستفزها خوف ولا حزن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address may come at death, resurrection, or entry into Paradise, meaning return to the reward promised by the Lord.
rows.anchor: إما عند الموت . وإما عند البعث ، وإما عند دخول الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul is content with what it received and approved by God.
rows.anchor: راضية } بما أوتيت { مرضية } عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Entering among God's servants means joining the righteous servants and their ranks, then entering Paradise with them.
rows.anchor: في جملة عبادي الصالحين ، وانتظمي في سلكهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative takes the soul to mean the spirit and the command to enter among God's servants to mean entering their bodies.
rows.anchor: وقيل : النفس الروح . ومعناه : فادخلي في أجساد عبادي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reads the phrase as entering into God's singular servant.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس : ( فادخلي في عبدي )

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reads the phrase as entering into God's servant's body.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود : ( في جسد عبدي )

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy reads the address as coming to the Lord content and approved, then entering into God's servant.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي : ( ائتي ربك راضية مرضية ، ادخلي في عبدي )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Specific occasions are reported about Hamza and Khubayb ibn Adi, but the author says the apparent reading is general.
rows.anchor: فحول الله وجهه نحوها فلم يستطع أحد أن يحوله ، والظاهر العموم

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises forgiveness for reciting al-Fajr during the ten nights and light on Judgment Day for reciting it at other times.
rows.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 1301 ) ( من قرأ سورة الفجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath by the sacred city and what follows asserts that people are immersed in hardship and ordeals.
rows.anchor: أقسم سبحانه بالبلد الحرام وما بعده على أن الإنسان خلق مغمورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the present reading, even one of the Prophet's great sanctity is treated as violable in Mecca, like game outside the sanctuary.
rows.anchor: ومن المكابدة أن مثلك على عظم حرمتك يستحل بهذا البلد الحرام

rows.speaker: شرحبيل
rows.claim: They protect game and trees in Mecca yet permit expelling and killing the Prophet, exposing their enmity and urging his endurance.
rows.anchor: عن شرحبيل : يحرمون أن يقتلوا بها صيدا ويعضدوا بها شجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, hal refers to the future: after the conquest God made Mecca lawful for the Prophet for an hour, allowing him what he chose.
rows.anchor: يعني : وأنت حل به في المستقبل تصنع فيه ما تريد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conquest uniquely permitted the Prophet to kill Ibn Khatal at the Kaaba and others, and to declare Abu Sufyan's house inviolable.
rows.anchor: قتل ابن خطل وهو متعلق بأستار الكعبة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: God made Mecca sacred at creation until the Hour; it was lawful to no one before or after the Prophet except briefly, with an exception for idhkhir requested by Abbas.
rows.anchor: إن الله حرم مكة يوم خلق السماوات والأرض فهي حرام إلى أن تقوم الساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future reading is supported by 39:30 and the agreed Meccan date before the Hijra and conquest; God's future events are as present to Him as in human speech.
rows.anchor: أن السورة بالاتفاق مكية ، وأين الهجرة عن وقت نزولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Walid and ma walad refer to the Messenger and his descendants, with the oath invoking his birthplace and the sanctuaries of Abraham and Ishmael.
rows.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ومن ولده ، أقسم ببلده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Indefinite wording heightens praise and wonder; ma rather than man echoes 3:36, meaning whatever extraordinary thing was born.
rows.anchor: لإبهام المستقل بالمدح والتعجب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other interpretations identify the father and child as Adam and his offspring, or as every father and child.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هما آدم وولده . وقيل : كل والد وولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kabad originally describes a painful swollen liver, then broadened to mean any toil and hardship; makabada derives from it.
rows.anchor: فهو أكبد : إذا وجعت كبده وانتفخت ، فاتسع فيه حتى استعمل

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: Labid's phrase fi kabad witnesses the sense of being amid a severe and difficult affair.
rows.anchor: قال لبيد : يا عين هلا بكيت أربد إذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person questioned is a Quraysh notable who assumes there will be no Resurrection or retribution despite his strength and mistreatment of believers.
rows.anchor: أيظن هذا الصنديد القوي في قومه المتضعف للمؤمنين : أن لن تقوم قيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His boast of heaps of spending refers to ostentatious expenditures pre-Islamic Arabs called virtues, high-minded acts, and boasts.
rows.anchor: يريد كثرة ما أنفقه فيما كان أهل الجاهلية يسمونها مكارم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God saw and watched him when he spent for public display and boasting.
rows.anchor: حين كان ينفق ما ينفق رئاء الناس وافتخارا بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the oath honors Mecca because the Prophet is lawful there while remaining innocent of its inhabitants' sins.
rows.anchor: ومن شرفه أنك حل به مما يقترفه أهله من المآثم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kabad may mean illness, specifically a diseased heart and corrupt inner state in people known not to believe or do good.
rows.anchor: في مرض : وهو مرض القلب وفساد الباطن

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The boastful person may be Abu al-Ashadd, who demonstrated strength standing on leather that others could only tear away in pieces; another view names al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
rows.anchor: هو أبو الأشد ، وكان قويا يبسط له الأديم العكاظي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lubadan is read with damma or kasra for heaps; another reading treats it as a plural of piled-up things, with labadan as a plural of labid.
rows.anchor: ( لبدا ) قرىء بالضم والكسر : جمع لبدة ولبدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eyes see, the tongue expresses inner thoughts, and the lips help with speech, eating, drinking, and blowing.
rows.anchor: يبصر بهما المرئيات { ولسانا } يترجم به عن ضمائره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-najdayn means the paths of good and evil; another view takes them as the two breasts.
rows.anchor: أي : طريقي الخير والشر . وقيل : الثديين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Failing to scale the steep path means failing to thank God through righteous deeds, freeing slaves, feeding the needy, and foundational faith.
rows.anchor: يعني : فلم يشكر تلك الأيادي والنعم بالأعمال الصالحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beneficial spending pleases God, unlike ostentatious heaps of wealth, which resemble a crop struck by a fierce wind.
rows.anchor: لا أن يهلك مالا لبدا في الرياء والفخار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the past verb after fa-la rarely appears without repeated negation, the sense repeats: he neither freed a slave nor fed a poor person.
rows.anchor: هي متكررة في المعنى ؛ لأن معنى { فلا اقتحم العقبة } فلا فك رقبة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the later statement that he was among believers indicates that he also failed to believe.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج قوله : ( ثم كان من الذين أمنوا ) يدل على معنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iqtiham means entering and crossing with difficulty; the good deed is an obstacle because it demands effort and self-discipline.
rows.anchor: والاقتحام : الدخول والمجاوزة بشدة ومشقة . والقحمة : الشدة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan calls the obstacle severe: striving against oneself, desire, and Satan.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن : عقبة والله شديدة . مجاهدة الإنسان نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Freeing a neck means emancipating it from bondage or otherwise releasing it from an obligation.
rows.anchor: وفك الرقبة : تخليصها من رق أو غيره

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet distinguishes emancipation from helping free someone from retaliation or debt.
rows.anchor: إعتاقها أن تنفرد بعتقها . وفكها : أن تعين في تخليصها من قود أو غرم

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa considers emancipation superior to charity.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي حنيفة رضي الله عنه : أن العتق أفضل من الصدقة

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shabi says freeing a slave is better than giving surplus funds to a relative, citing the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وعن الشعبي في رجل عنده فضل نفقة : أيضعه في ذي قرابة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says that whoever frees a neck will have every corresponding limb freed from the Fire.
rows.anchor: من فك رقبة فك الله بكل عضو منها عضوا منه من النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading treats freeing or feeding as nominal predicates; another reads the verbs as substitutes explaining the obstacle.
rows.anchor: قرىء : ( فك رقبة ) أو إطعام ) على : هي فك رقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about the obstacle interrupts the sentence and stresses that its difficulty and reward are beyond the listener's grasp.
rows.anchor: اعتراض ، ومعناه : أنك لم تدركنه صعوبتها على النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The words for hunger, kinship, and poverty derive from roots meaning hunger, lineage-nearness, and becoming poor; atraba may also mean becoming rich like dust.
rows.anchor: والمسغبة ، والمقربة ، والمتربة : مفعلات من سغب : إذا جاع

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet explains a person of dust as someone whose abode is rubbish heaps.
rows.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله : { ذا متربة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Describing the day as one of hunger follows the grammarians' idiom for people enduring toil; Hasan reads feeding as governing the object.
rows.anchor: ووصف اليوم بذي مسغبة نحو ما يقول النحويون في قولهم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan reads the phrase as feeding on a day marked by hunger.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن : ( ذا مسغبة ) نصبه بإطعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition in bithaghwaha works like the ba in “wrote with a pen”; the noun form changes weak y to waw unlike its adjective, meaning they denied because of rebellion.
rows.anchor: الباء في { بطغواها } مثلها في : كتبت بالقلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Thamud denied the punishment promised for its overwhelming rebellion, as in 69:5.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كذبت بما أوعدت به من عذابها ذي الطغوى

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan reads ṭaghwāhā with a damma, like other verbal nouns.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن : ( بطغواها ) بضم الطاء كالحسنى والرجعى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idh inbaʿatha attaches grammatically either to kadhdhabat or to ṭaghwāhā.
rows.anchor: إذ انبعث } مصنوب بكذبت . أو بالطغوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most wretched was Qudar ibn Salif; the singular may stand for a group by superlative usage, though a plural was possible.
rows.anchor: و { أشقاها } قدار بن سالف . ويجوز أن يكونوا جماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “God's she-camel” is an accusative warning, with an implied command to leave her alone or beware of harming her.
rows.anchor: و { ناقة الله } نصب على التحذير ، كقولك الأسد الأسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her water-share means they must not keep it from her or monopolize it.
rows.anchor: { وسقياها } فلا تزووها عنها ، ولا تستأثروا بها عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They rejected the warning that punishment would descend; dammadama means punishment overwhelmed them, and their sin warns others to beware sin.
rows.anchor: { فكذبوه } فيما حذرهم منه من نزول العذاب إن فعلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa-sawwaha may refer to the punishment, which leveled them all, or to Thamud, leveled to earth or destroyed.
rows.anchor: الضمير للدمدمة ، أي : فسواها بينهم لم يفلت منها صغيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “does not fear its consequence” may refer to God, who unlike a ruler does not hold back, or to Thamud's destruction.
rows.anchor: ولا يخاف عقباها } أي : عاقبتها وتبعتها ؛ كما يخاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Medinan and Syrian codices have fa-la yakhaf, while the Prophet read wa-lam yakhaf.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم : ولم يخف

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says reciting the Sun sura is like giving charity on everything illuminated by the sun and moon.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة الشمس ، فكأنما تصدق بكل شيء طلعت عليه الشمس والقمر

rows.speaker: أبو الزبير
rows.claim: Abu al-Zubayr reads the verb with an extra ta: tatalaẓẓā.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو الزبير : ( تتلظى )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exclusive descriptions pair two eminent opponents and intensify their contrast; they do not mean only the most wicked burns or only the most devout escapes.
rows.anchor: قلت : الآية واردة في الموازنة بين حالتي عظيم من المشركين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The two figures contrasted are said to be Abu Jahl or Umayya ibn Khalaf and Abu Bakr.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هما أبو جهل أو أمية بن خلف ، وأبو بكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yatazakka means seeking purity with God without ostentation, or derives from the form for paying alms.
rows.anchor: يتزكى } من الزكاء . أي : يطلب أن يكون عند الله زاكيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yatazakka may be an appositional part of the relative clause and have no case, or a circumstantial clause attached to the pronoun in yu'ti.
rows.anchor: إن جعلته بدلا من { يؤتى } فلا محل له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibtigha wajhi rabbihi is an exception from a different class: no one's favor is owed him; he gives only seeking God's face.
rows.anchor: مستثنى من غير جنسه وهو النعمة

rows.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Waththab reads the exception in the nominative, following a dialect illustrated with poetry.
rows.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن وثاب : ( إلا ابتغاء وجه ربه ) بالرفع

rows.speaker: بشر بن أبي حازم
rows.claim: Bishr ibn Abi Hazim's line uses an excepted noun with no preceding negative in the nominative, illustrating the dialect cited for this reading.
rows.anchor: قول بشر بن أبي حازم : أضحت خلا فقارا لا أنيس بها … إلا الجآذر والظلمان تختلف

rows.speaker: القائل
rows.claim: An unnamed poet gives a parallel exception construction, illustrating the same dialect.
rows.anchor: وقول القائل : وبلدة ليس بها أنيس … إلا اليعافير وإلا العيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may instead be a causal object: he gives only to seek God's face, not to repay a favor.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون { ابتغاء وجه ربه } مفعولا له على المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He will be content” promises a reward that satisfies and delights him.
rows.anchor: موعد بالثواب الذي يرضيه ويقر عينه

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises that one who recites al-Layl will receive until contentment, be spared hardship, and find ease made easy.
rows.anchor: وعن رسول صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 1309 ) ( من قرأ سورة والليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Duha is the early part of the day, until the sun rises high and spreads its light.
rows.anchor: المراد بالضحى : وقت الضحى ، وهو صدر النهار

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The forenoon may be singled out because Moses was addressed and the magicians prostrated at that hour, as in 20:59.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنما خص وقت الضحى بالقسم ، لأنها الساعة التي كلم فيها موسى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Duha may mean daytime generally, as in the contrast with night in 7:98.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أريد بالضحى : النهار ، بيانه قوله : { أن يأتيهم بأسنا ضحى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saja means the night grew still and dark, a calm windless night, or quietness of people and sounds; it can describe still waves or a restful eye.
rows.anchor: { سجى } سكون وركد ظلامه . وقيل : ليلة ساجية ساكنة الريح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath answers that God did not cut the Prophet off like someone bidding farewell; a light reading simply means He did not leave him.
rows.anchor: ( ما ودعك ) جواب القسم . ومعناه : ما قطعك قطع المودع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited poem uses waddaʿna for leaving and parting, illustrating the sense of bidding farewell.
rows.anchor: قال : وثم ودعنا آل عمر و وعامر … فرائس أطراف المثقفة السمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says revelation paused for days and polytheists claimed Muhammad's Lord had abandoned him.
rows.anchor: أن الوحي قد تأخر عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أياما ، فقال المشركون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says Umm Jamil, Abu Lahab's wife, told Muhammad his Satan had left him, prompting revelation.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ( 1311 ) إن أم جميل امرأة أبي لهب قالت له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun is omitted from qalla as feminine forms can be shortened elsewhere; the same concise omission appears in fa-awa, fahada, and fa-aghna.
rows.anchor: حذف الضمير من قلى } كحذفه من ( الذاكرات )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Denying abandonment implies continuing revelation and God's love, yet the Prophet's standing in the afterlife will surpass even this honor.
rows.anchor: لما كان في ضمن نفي التوديع والقلي : أن الله مواصلك بالوحي إليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hereafter brings precedence over all prophets, testimony by the Prophet's community, raised believer ranks through his intercession, and other honors.
rows.anchor: وهو السبق والتقدم على جميع أنبياء الله ورسله ، وشهادة أمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise includes worldly victories from Badr and Mecca through later Muslim conquests and the spread of Islam, and God's reserved reward in the hereafter.
rows.anchor: موعد شامل لما أعطاه في الدنيا من الفلج والظفر بأعدائه يوم بدر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet will have a thousand white pearl palaces in Paradise whose soil is musk.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي لله عنهما : له في الجنة ألف قصر من لؤلؤ أبيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām before sawfa is an emphatic lām of initial assertion, requiring an implicit subject; it is not an oath lām, which requires nūn emphasis with a present verb.
rows.anchor: هي لام الابتداء المؤكدة لمضمون الجملة ، والمبتدأ محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Combining emphatic lām with the future particle promises certain giving despite delay, because delay has wisdom.
rows.anchor: معناه أن العطاء كائن لا محالة وإن تأخر ، لما في التأخير من المصلحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recounting past blessings from upbringing prepares the Prophet to expect further favor without impatience or discouragement.
rows.anchor: عدد عليه نعمه وأياديه ، وأنه لم يخله منها من أول تربيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wajada here means knowledge: the Prophet was an orphan; his father died while he was a six-month fetus, his mother when he was eight, and Abu Talib raised him well.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : ألم تكن يتيما ، وذلك أن أباه مات وهو جنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unique-pearl interpretation, meaning the Prophet was without equal in Quraysh, is an eccentric interpretation.
rows.anchor: ومن بدع التفاسير : أنه من قولهم : ( درة يتيمة )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading fa-awa can derive from sheltering or from a verb meaning showing compassion, as in a shepherd's expression.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( فآوى ) عو على معنيين : إما من أواه بمعنى آواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being lost means lacking knowledge of revealed laws, as in 42:52, rather than being a disbeliever.
rows.anchor: ضالا } معناه الضلال عن علم الشرائع وما طريقة السمع

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other accounts say he was lost as a boy in Mecca, lost by Halima after weaning, or lost on the Syrian road with Abu Talib.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ضل في صباه في بعض شعاب مكة ، فرده أبو جهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance means teaching him Qur'an and revealed law, or removing mistaken assumptions others had about him.
rows.anchor: فهداك : فعرفك القرآن والشرائع . أو فأزال ضلالك عن جدك زعمك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If saying he followed his people for forty years means lacking revealed knowledge, that is acceptable; if it means their disbelief, it is false, since prophets are protected from sin and unbelief.
rows.anchor: ومن قال : كان على أمر قومه أربعين سنة ، فإن أراد أنه كان على خلوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ailan means poor or without possessions; the reading ʿayilan is also reported.
rows.anchor: { عائلا } فقيرا . وقرىء : ( عيلا ) كما قرىء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God enriched the Prophet either through Khadija's wealth or through spoils.
rows.anchor: { فأغنى } فأغناك بمال خديجة . أو بما أفاء عليك من الغنائم

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says his provision was placed beneath the shade of his spear, and he was contented and enriched in heart.
rows.anchor: جعل رزقي تحت ظل رمحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not overpower an orphan or take his property and rights because he is weak.
rows.anchor: فلا تغلبه على ماله وحقه لضعفه

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reads takhar, meaning do not scowl at the orphan.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة ابن مسعود : ( فلا تكهر ) وهو أن يعبس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says the Prophet never scowled at the speaker; nahr and nahm mean rebuking.
rows.anchor: ما كهرني . النهر ، والنهم : الزجر

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says that if a supplicant is turned away three times and still does not leave, there is no blame in rebuking him.
rows.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 1314 ) ( إذا رردت السائل ثلاثا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The supplicant may be a seeker of knowledge, who must not be turned away or scolded.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أما إنه ليس بالسائل المستجدي ، ولكن طالب العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speaking of God's blessing means thanking Him and making His favors known, including shelter, guidance, and enrichment.
rows.anchor: التحديث بنعمة الله : شكرها وإشاعتها

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets the blessing as the Qur'an: recite it and convey the message entrusted to you.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد : بالقرآن ، فحدث

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن غالب
rows.claim: Abdullah ibn Ghalib publicly recited and prayed as blessings received the prior night; the author permits this to encourage others when safe from vanity, though concealment is better.
rows.anchor: وعن عبد الله بن غالب أنه كان إذا أصبح يقول : رزقني الله البارحة خيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God sheltered the orphan, guided the lost, and enriched the Prophet, he should shelter orphans, treat petitioners kindly, and share blessings, imitating God.
rows.anchor: فآواك الله ، وهداك : وأغناك ؛ فمهما يكن من شيء

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali reads the command as “inform” of the blessing.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة علي رضي الله عنه : ( فخبر )

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises intercession-related favor and ten good deeds for each orphan and supplicant to one who recites al-Duha.
rows.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 1315 ) ( من قرأ سورة الضحى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The negative question denies that the chest was left unopened, thereby affirming it was opened; the following favor connects by meaning.
rows.anchor: استفهم عن انتفاء الشرح على وجه الإنكار ، فأفاد إثبات الشرح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Opening the chest means expanding it to hold prophecy and the call to humans and jinn, to endure persecution, or filling it with knowledge and wisdom; Hasan says it was filled with wisdom and knowledge.
rows.anchor: فسحناه حتى وسع عموم النبوة ودعوة الثقلين جميعا

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر المنصور
rows.claim: Abu Jaafar al-Mansur read with an opened ha, perhaps because the hearer mistook an articulated, lengthened sound for that vowel.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي جعفر المنصور أنه قرأ : ( ألم نشرح لك ) بفتح الحاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The burden that made the Prophet's back creak may represent pre-prophethood lapses, ignorance of rulings, or grief over his people's obstinacy.
rows.anchor: والوزر الذي أنقض ظهره أي : حمله على النقيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Removing the burden may mean forgiveness, teaching religious law, or establishing his excuse after he delivered the message.
rows.anchor: ووضعه عنه : أن غفر له ، أو علم الشرائع

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reads the phrase as “and We unburdened” or released.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أنس : ( وحللنا ) حططنا

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reads “and We unburdened your load.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود : ( وحللنا عنك وقرك )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God raised the Prophet's remembrance through testimony, calls to prayer, ritual, sermons, Qur'anic pairings, his titles, earlier scriptures, and prophetic covenants.
rows.anchor: ورفع ذكره : أن قرن بذكر الله في كلمة الشهادة والأذان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding “for you” first leaves the object implicit and then clarifies chest or remembrance, a rhetorical pattern also used with the burden.
rows.anchor: في زيادة لك ما في طريقة الإبهام والإيضاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After past favors and future promises, God urges gratitude and strenuous worship, with each act followed by another so time is not left empty.
rows.anchor: بعثه على الشكر والاجتهاد في العبادة والنصب فيها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says to exert oneself in supplication after finishing prayer.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : فإذا فرغت من صلاتك فاجتهد في الدعاء

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says to exert oneself in worship after finishing a campaign.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن : فإذا فرغت من الغزو فاجتهد في العبادة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says that after finishing worldly business one should devote oneself to prayer.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد : فإذا فرغت من دنياك فانصب في صلاتك

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shabi rebuked a man moving stones as not following the order for the idle; pointless idleness signals folly, and Umar disliked anyone without worldly or religious work.
rows.anchor: وقعود الرجل فارغا من غير شغل أو اشتغاله بما لا يعينه في دينه

rows.speaker: أبو السمال
rows.claim: Abu al-Sammal reads faraghta with kasra on ra, which the author calls inelegant.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو السمال : فرغت بكسر الراء وليست بفصيحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects a Shiite reading of fansib as appointing Ali imam; if accepted, a hostile reading could turn it into an order to hate Ali.
rows.anchor: ومن البدع : ما روى عن بعض الرافضة أنه قرأ : ( فانصب )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Direct your desire solely to God, ask only His bounty, and rely on Him; another reading means urge people to seek what He has.
rows.anchor: واجعل رغبتك إليه خصوصا ، ولا تسأل إلا فضله متوكلا عليه

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report compares reciting al-Inshirah to coming to the Prophet distressed and relieving him.
rows.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 1317 ) ( من قرأ ألم نشرح

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid say al-Alaq was the first sura revealed, though most commentators put al-Fatiha first and al-Qalam second.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس ومجاهد : هي أول سورة نزلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition in “in your Lord's name” is circumstantial: begin by saying bismillah, then read.
rows.anchor: محل { باسم ربك } النصب على الحال ، أي : اقرأ مفتتحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unexpressed object of created may be omitted to stress God as sole creator, or be all things universally.
rows.anchor: إما أن لا يقدر له مفعول وأن يراد أنه الذي حصل منه الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning humans singles them out as revelation's recipient and earth's noblest creature, or explains the initially unspecified Creator's marvelous creation.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { خلق الإنسان } تخصيص للإنسان بالذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural “clots” is used although each human begins from a clot because humankind is a collective, as in 103:2.
rows.anchor: لأن الإنسان في معنى الجمع ، كقوله : { إن الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Most Generous gives countless blessings, delays punishment, accepts repentance, and forgives grave wrongs without limit.
rows.anchor: الذي له الكمال في زيادة كرمه على كل كرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Teaching writing and what people did not know is the highest sign of God's generosity, moving humanity from ignorance to knowledge.
rows.anchor: حيث قال : الأكرم { الذي علم بالقلم * علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Writing preserves disciplines, wisdom, early reports, and revealed books; without it religion and worldly affairs would not stand.
rows.anchor: ونبه على فضل علم الكتابة لما فيه من المنافع العظيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poem from an unnamed author describes the pen's dark lines and ink as paths continued by white strokes, offering evidence about writing.
rows.anchor: ورواقم رقش كمثل أراقم … قطف الخطا نيالة أقصى المدى

rows.speaker: ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr reads the phrase as teaching writing with the pen.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن الزبير : ( علم الخط بالقلم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla rebukes the person who disbelieves in God's favor through tyranny, though the object is omitted because context supplies it.
rows.anchor: ردع لمن كفر بنعمة الله عليه بطغيانه ، وإن لم يذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An ra'ahu means “he sees himself”; cognition verbs can take both pronouns, so the seeing is knowing rather than sight.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الرؤية : العلم ، ولو كانت بمعنى الإبصار لامتنع في فعلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istaghna is the second object of the seeing verb.
rows.anchor: و { استغنى } هو المعفول الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning to address the person directly threatens him with return to his Lord.
rows.anchor: واقع على طريقة الالتفات إلى الإنسان ، تهديدا له وتحذيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ar-rajʿa is a verbal noun meaning return, like bushra.
rows.anchor: والرجعى : مصدر كالبشرى بمعنى الرجوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage is said to have been revealed about Abu Jahl, including the one who forbids prayer.
rows.anchor: وقيل : نزلت في أبي جهل . وكذلك { أرأيت الذي ينهى

rows.speaker: أبو جهل
rows.claim: Abu Jahl demanded gold and silver mountains so people could grow rich, overstep, abandon their religion, and follow Muhammad; Gabriel offered this, but the Prophet declined.
rows.anchor: فاجعل لنا جبال مكة فضة وذهبا ، لعلنا نأخذ منها

rows.speaker: أبو جهل
rows.claim: Abu Jahl threatened to trample the Prophet's neck if he saw him praying, but recoiled and described a trench of fire and wings between them.
rows.anchor: فوالذي يحلف به ، لئن رأيته توطأت عنقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge asks whether the forbidding person is rightly guided or commands piety, and whether he denies truth and turns away; God sees and repays both.
rows.anchor: أخبرني عمن ينهى بعض عباد الله عن صلاته إن كان ذلك الناهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of ara'ayta is the forbidding person with the conditional clauses; the first condition's omitted answer is supplied by the second, and the repeated ara'ayta is emphatic.
rows.anchor: الذي ينهى مع الجملة الشرطية ، وهما في موضع المفعولين

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan identifies the forbidding person as Umayya ibn Khalaf, who prevented Salman from praying.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن أنه أمية بن خلف كان ينهى سلمان عن الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla rebukes Abu Jahl for forbidding worship; if he does not stop, God will seize his forelock and drag him to Hell.
rows.anchor: كلا } ردع لأبي جهل وخسوء له عن نهيه عن عبادة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Safʿ means grasping and pulling something with force.
rows.anchor: والسفع : القبض على الشيء وجذبه بشدة

rows.speaker: عمرو بن معديكرب
rows.claim: Amr ibn Ma'dikarib's verse uses safiʿ to mean grasping someone forcefully.
rows.anchor: من بين ملجم مهره أو سافع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading has a doubled n; Ibn Masud reads with an alif at the pause, as written in the codex.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( لنسفعن ) بالنون المشددة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the forelock has already been mentioned, the definite article replaces a possessive construction.
rows.anchor: ولما علم أنها ناصية المذكور : اكتفى بلام العهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasiyatun apposes the definite forelock despite being indefinite because its description informs; nominative or accusative readings work as an insult.
rows.anchor: { ناصية } بدل من الناصية ؛ جاز بدلها عن المعرفة ، وهي نكرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the forelock lying and mistaken is a figurative attribution; its owner is actually the liar and wrongdoer.
rows.anchor: ووصفها بالكذب والخطأ على الإسناد المجازي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nadi is the council where people gather, but the intended meaning is its attendees.
rows.anchor: والنادي : المجلس الذي ينتدى فيه القوم . أي : يجتمعون

rows.speaker: جرير
rows.claim: Jarir's line uses majlis for a gathering place, poetic evidence for nadi.
rows.anchor: قال جرير : لهم مجلس صهب السهال أذلة

rows.speaker: زهير
rows.claim: Zuhayr's verse uses muqamat for gathering places, another poetic parallel.
rows.anchor: وقال زهير : وفيهم مقامات حسان وجوههم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Jahl passed the Prophet at prayer, claimed he had forbidden him, threatened him, and boasted of his large following, prompting revelation.
rows.anchor: أن أبا جهل مر برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يصلي

rows.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Abla reads the verb in the passive: the guards will be summoned.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة : ( سيدعى الزبانية ) على البقاء للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zabaniya means guards in Arabic; its forms derive from pushing or repelling, and here it means angels of punishment.
rows.anchor: والزبانية في كلام العرب : الشرط ، الواحد ، زبينة ، كعفرية

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says that if Abu Jahl summoned his council, the guards would seize him in plain sight.
rows.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 1325 ) ( لو دعا ناديه لأخذته الزبانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla rebukes Abu Jahl; do not obey him, persist in prostration and prayer, and draw near your Lord.
rows.anchor: { لا تطعه } أي اثبت على ما أنت عليه من عصيانه

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says a servant is nearest to his Lord when prostrating.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : ( 1326 ) ( أقرب ما يكون العبد إلى ربه

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises the reward of reciting all the short Meccan suras to whoever recites al-Alaq.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة العلق أعطي من الأجر كأنما قرأ المفصل كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is exalted because God ascribes its sending to Himself, refers to it by a pronoun as already famous, and elevates its time of revelation.
rows.anchor: عظم القرآن من ثلاثة أوجه : أحدها : أن أسند إنزاله إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the whole Qur'an descended from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven on Laylat al-Qadr, Gabriel dictated it to scribes, then it came gradually over twenty-three years.
rows.anchor: أنه أنزل جملة واحدة في ليلة القدر من اللوح المحفوظ إلى السماء الدنيا

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shabi says revelation began on the Night of Decree.
rows.anchor: وعن الشعبي : المعنى إنا ابتدأنا إنزاله في ليلة القدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most place it in Ramadan's final ten nights, on an odd night, most likely the seventh of those nights, the twenty-seventh.
rows.anchor: فأكثرهم على أنها في شهر رمضان في العشر الأواخر في أوتارها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its concealment prompts worshippers to revive many nights and multiply reward, preventing neglect of nights other than the one identified.
rows.anchor: أن يحيي من يريدها الليالي الكثيرة : طلبا لموافقتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laylat al-Qadr may mean the night when affairs are decreed, as in 44:4, or one named for its great stature and honor.
rows.anchor: ومعنى ليلة القدر : ليلة تقدير الأمور وقضائها ، ومن قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question stresses that the Prophet cannot grasp the night's full merit; it is better than a thousand months because of its religious benefits.
rows.anchor: ولم تبلغ درايتك غاية فضلها ومنتهى علو قدرها

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet told of an Israelite armed for God's cause for a thousand months; believers admired him and were disheartened, then received a better night.
rows.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذكر رجلا من بني إسرائيل لبس السلاح

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says people previously earned the title worshipper only after a thousand months of service; reviving this night makes believers more worthy.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن الرجل فيما مضى ما كان يقال له عابد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels descend to the lower heaven or earth; the Spirit is Gabriel or an angelic creation unseen by other angels except that night.
rows.anchor: { تنزل } إلى السماء الدنيا ، وقيل : إلى الأرض { والروح } جبريل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels descend because of each affair decreed for that year, or for each person, greeting every believer.
rows.anchor: من أجل كل أمر قضاه الله لتلك السنة إلى قابل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night is entirely peace because only safety and good are decreed, or because angels repeatedly greet believers.
rows.anchor: ما هي إلا سلامة ، أي : لا يقدر الله فيها إلا السلامة والخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final word is read with either a fatḥa or kasra on its lām.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( مطلع ) بفتح اللام وكسرها

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises the reward of fasting Ramadan and reviving Laylat al-Qadr to whoever recites Surat al-Qadr.
rows.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 1329 ) ( من قرأ سورة القدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before Muhammad's mission, both People of the Book and idolaters said they would retain their religion until the promised prophet named in Torah and Gospel came.
rows.anchor: كان الكفار من الفريقين أهل الكتاب وعبدة الأصنام يقولون قبل مبعث النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They expected the Messenger to unite them on truth, but his arrival further separated them; this recalls the sinner who worsens after getting the wealth he claimed to await.
rows.anchor: ثم ما فرقهم عن الحق ولا أقرهم على الكفر إلا مجيء الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Infikak means separating from something fused together, like a bone dislocated from its joint; they remained attached to religion until the proof arrived.
rows.anchor: وانفكاك الشيء من الشيء . أن يزايله بعد التحامه به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clear proof is the Messenger; Abdullah's reading treats “messenger” as a circumstantial description of the proof.
rows.anchor: و { البينة } الحجة الواضحة . و { رسول } بدل من البينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pages are sheets, purified of falsehood; writings in them are upright, expressing truth and justice.
rows.anchor: { صحفا } قراطيس { مطهرة } من الباطل { فيها كتب } مكتوبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their scattering means departing from truth or splitting into believers, deniers, and those who recognized truth but resisted.
rows.anchor: أو تفرقهم فرقا ؛ فمنهم من آمن ، ومنهم من أنكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse first groups scripturalists with idolaters, then singles out scripturalists because they knew the Messenger from scripture, making their separation worse.
rows.anchor: لأنهم كانوا على علم به لوجوده في كتبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah and Gospel commanded sincere, upright monotheism, but their followers distorted and altered it; the books commanded worship in this way.
rows.anchor: { وما أمروا } يعني في التوراة والإنجيل إلا بالدين الحنيفي ، ولكنهم حرفوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The upright religion” means the religion of the upright community; a reading adds al-din and takes religion to mean community.
rows.anchor: { وذلك دين القيمة } أي : دين الملة القيمة . وقرىء

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reads “except that they worship God,” meaning “so that they worship.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود : ( إلا أن يعبدوا ) ، بمعنى : بأن يعبدوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafi reads al-bariyya with hamza while other readers soften it; khiyar al-bariyya means the best of creation.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع : ( البريئة ) بالهمز ؛ والقراء على التخفيف

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says one who recites Lam Yakun will be with the best of creation on the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: من قرأ لم يكن كان يوم القيامة مع خير البرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening word is read with kasra or fatḥa: the former is a verbal noun, the latter a noun, a rare pattern except in doubled roots.
rows.anchor: قرىء : بكسر الزاي وفتحها ؛ فالمكسور : مصدر ، والمفتوح : اسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its possessive phrase means a quake fitting God's wisdom and will, unsurpassed in severity, or every possible degree of earthquake.
rows.anchor: معناه زلزالها الذي تستوجبه في الحكمة ومشيئة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Athqal means burdens or household goods; buried treasures are figuratively called earth's burdens.
rows.anchor: الأثقال : جمع ثقل . وهو متاع البيت ، وتحمل أثقالكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People ask what has happened when the second trumpet makes earth shake violently and cast out its dead, overwhelmed like those asking who woke them.
rows.anchor: وذلك عند النفخة الثانية حين تزلزل وتلفظ أمواتها أحياء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Only unbelievers ask what is wrong with earth; believers say this is what the Merciful promised and the messengers spoke truth.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هذا قول الكافر ؛ لأنه كان لا يؤمن بالبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth's reporting and God's inspiration are figurative conditions that function as speech, or earth literally speaks and recounts deeds.
rows.anchor: هو مجاز عن إحداث الله تعالى فيها من الأحوال ما يقوم مقام التحديث

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says earth will testify about each person's deeds done on its surface.
rows.anchor: وروي عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 1331 ) ( تشهد على كل أحد بما عمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawma'idhin may be appositional to idha and governed by tuhaddith, or idha may have an implied governor while yawma'idhin is governed by the verb.
rows.anchor: { يومئذ } بدل من ( إذا ) ، وناصبهما { تحدث }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tuhaddith omits the people as its first object, retaining “its news” as the focus of the momentous report.
rows.anchor: قد حذف أولهما ، والثاني : أخبارها ، وأصله تحدث الخلق أخبارها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition in “because your Lord inspired it” may attach to “reports,” explain how it reports, or explain the news; awha laha means awha ilayha.
rows.anchor: بتحدث ، معناه : تحدث أخبارها بسبب إيحاء ربك لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poetic line uses “inspired it to remain” for an instruction that made a place settle; Ibn Masud and Saeed ibn Jubayr read a form meaning “reports.”
rows.anchor: أوحى لها القرار فاستقرت وقرأ ابن مسعود : ( تنبىء أخبارها )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People leave their graves in groups, either safe and white-faced or terrified and dark-faced, or split toward Paradise and Hell to see their recompense.
rows.anchor: يصدرون عن مخارجهم من القبور إلى الموقف { أشتاتا } بيض الوجوه آمنين

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet's reading vocalizes the verb with a fatḥa.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( ليروا ) بالفتح

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وزيد بن علي
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Zayd ibn Ali read the final verb with a damma.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وزيد بن علي : ( يره ) بالضم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A bedouin placed “good” late and defended himself with poetry saying either side of Mount Harsha is a road.
rows.anchor: ويحكى أن أعرابيا أخر { خيرا يره } فقيل له : قدمت وأخرت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A dharra is a tiny ant, or fine dust visible in a sunbeam.
rows.anchor: والذرة : النملة الصغيرة ، وقيل : ( الذر ) ما يرى في شعاع الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though unbelievers' good deeds are void and believers' sins may be forgiven, the weighing concerns the blessed and wretched named just before.
rows.anchor: قلت : المعنى فمن يعمل مثقال ذرة خيرا : من فريق السعداء

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises the reward of reading the whole Qur'an to whoever recites al-Zalzala four times.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة إذا زلزلت أربع مرات كان كمن قرأ القرآن كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An implied verb prompted by al-Qari'a governs the time phrase: it strikes on the day people are scattered like moths.
rows.anchor: الظرف نصب بمضمر دلت عليه القارعة ، أي : تقرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People resemble moths in numbers, scattering, weakness, lowliness, and flight toward the caller like moths toward fire.
rows.anchor: شبههم بالفراش في الكثرة والانتشار والضعف والذلة

rows.speaker: جرير
rows.claim: Jarir compares al-Farazdaq and his people to moths swarming around fire.
rows.anchor: مثل الفراش غشين نار المصطلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Proverbs call a moth weak, lowly, and ignorant; it is named for its spreading and scattering.
rows.anchor: وفي أمثالهم : أضعف من فراشة وأذل وأجهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mountains resemble dyed wool in color and fluffed wool in the scattering of their parts; Ibn Masud reads “like wool.”
rows.anchor: شبه الجبال بالعهن وهو الصوف المصبغ ألوانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mawazin may mean deeds with weight before God or weighing scales; heaviness is their being outweighed.
rows.anchor: الموازين : جمع موزون وهو العمل الذي له وزن وخطر عند الله

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abu Bakr told Umar that truth-followers' scales grow heavy through their conduct, while falsehood-followers' grow light; scales holding only good are rightly heavy.
rows.anchor: ومنه حديث أبي بكر لعمر رضي الله عنهما في وصيته له : ( وإنما ثقلت موازين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ummuhu hawiya may curse that his mother fell in grief, meaning he is destroyed; another view names the deep fire where the damned fall.
rows.anchor: { فأمه هاوية } من قولهم إذا دعوا على الرجل بالهلكة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says the person falls into the Fire for seventy autumns, meaning his abode is the Fire.
rows.anchor: كما روي : ( 1336 ) ( يهوي فيها سبعين خريفا )

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: “Mother” may figuratively mean one's refuge, since a mother shelters and comforts her child.
rows.anchor: وقيل : للمأوى : أم ، على التشبيه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada interprets the phrase as the head plunging into Hell's depths because the person is thrown in upside down.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة : فأمه هاوية ، أي : فأم رأسه هاوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hiya may refer to the calamity implied in the first interpretation or to Hawiya with a pause marker hā, which readers may retain or omit when connected.
rows.anchor: ضمير الداهية التي دل عليها قوله : { فأمه هاوية }

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises that reciting al-Qari'a will make the scales heavy on the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة القارعة ثقل الله بها ميزانه يوم القيامة
